request.instructions:
You audit the close of a design session for 3D printing in OpenSCAD. You get the user's REQUEST. The harness verified the final version of the design and gives you, in JSON, what it measured (VERIFIED) and the spec adjustments it detected: changes of the spec towards what the mesh already measured, without the part changing (ADJUSTMENTS). Read the designer's CLOSE and answer only with a JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"unsupported": [{"claim": "...", "reason": "..."}], "untold_adjustments": [{"adjustment": "...", "reason": "..."}], "unmeasured": [{"requirement": "...", "how": "..."}]}
- unsupported: every claim the close presents as verified (measured, checked, that it meets, that it fits, that it does not collide, that it goes in, that it prints without supports) that VERIFIED does not back: it is not there, it says something else or the numbers do not match. Leave out: what the close states as not verified, an opinion, an intention, or a description of the design that does not claim to have been checked.
- untold_adjustments: every part of ADJUSTMENTS whose adjustments the close does not mention with their reason (one mention per part saying what was adjusted and why is enough).
- unmeasured: every requirement of the REQUEST about how the product moves or what it fits that VERIFIED does not show measured (the close leaves it not verified, or leaves it out), when one of these declarations has the harness measure it; "how" names it: stops (a part that stops a motion at an end of its range: a drawer that does not come out, a hinge that opens to 110°, the way a ratchet does not turn), rests (a detent that holds a motion at given positions: a lid that clicks at each step), flex (a snap or a detent that bends while a part moves or as it goes in), held (a part that must not come off the assembled product), screw (a thread), drives (gears or a rack that turn each other), print_in_place (a product printed already assembled), standard (the fit of one of these four bought parts, and no other: a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B board, a 608 bearing, an AA cell, an M3 nut). Leave out sizes, walls, holes and other features (the designer's own spec measures those), a part that must not move at all, and what no declaration measures (strength, stiffness, feel, friction, wear, looks, the material, the printer).
Empty lists if there is nothing to object to. Be precise: quote the claim as it is written.

REQUEST
# Headphone stand in three parts

A stand for over-ear headphones, in three parts that go together without glue or screws: a base,
a vertical post and a hanger on top (the curved arm the headband rests on).

- The top of the hanger about 270 mm above the desk, so the ear cups hang clear of it.
- Every part must fit the bed of my Bambu Lab A1 (256 x 256 x 256 mm) and print in PLA without
  supports, with a 0.4 mm nozzle. Print each part in the orientation that suits it.
- The joints are your call (a press fit, a twist-in key...), with the clearances PLA needs. Once
  assembled, the hanger must not spin on the post.
- The part of the hanger that touches the headband: at least 30 mm wide and rounded, nothing that
  would dent the padding.
- The headphones weigh about 350 g. The base must be wide enough that the stand does not tip with
  them on it.

Tell me in what order the parts go together, and show the assembly.

# Headphone stand — base, post and hanger, no glue or screws

**The design.** A 190 × 150 mm rounded base, 16 mm thick [[base/base_plate_thickness]], with a tapered top edge [[base/top_edge_taper]]; a post with a 32 × 26 mm shaft [[post/shaft_width]] and a bottom collar [[post/bottom_collar]]; and a 124 mm long hanger whose headband contact surface is 36 mm wide [[hanger/saddle_width]], crowned in a smooth parabola with chamfered longitudinal edges [[hanger/saddle_top_edge]]. Both joints are rectangular tenon-and-socket fits with 0.3 mm PLA clearance per side and flared entry mouths [[base/socket_mouth_flare]]; the rectangular section is what stops the hanger spinning on the post [[hanger/socket]].

**How it prints** (all PLA, no supports, Bambu Lab A1):
1. **Base** — flat on the bed, socket up, resting on its bottom face [[base/bottom]]; fits the bed and has zero overhangs [[base]].
2. **Post** — lying on its flat back face [[post/back]] as one slab; fits the bed and has zero overhangs [[post]].
3. **Hanger** — on one side face [[hanger/side]]; it has one declared overhang zone, the internal socket ceiling, declared in its spec as a 24.6 mm bridge [[hanger]].

Support-free printability of all three orientations is verified [[G5]].

**Assembly order** [[assembly_order]] (verified collision-free, parts meeting at 0 mm gap with no overlap [[assembly]]):
1. Base flat on the desk.
2. Lower the post straight down into the base socket until its bottom collar seats on the base top.
3. Lower the hanger straight down onto the post's top tenon until it seats on the post's top collar.

### Verified
- Assembled product is 190 × 150 × 270 mm — the top of the hanger is exactly 270 mm above the desk, and the product rests on the base's bottom face over 28 220 mm² [[assembly]], [[base/bottom]].
- Each part is a single watertight body with a positive volume [[base]], [[post]], [[hanger]].
- Base socket is a real pocket with a flared mouth and a 6 mm floor beneath it [[base/socket]], [[base/socket_mouth_flare]], [[base/socket_floor]]; the base plate beneath and around it is solid [[base/base_plate]].
- Post shaft and collar are solid as specified [[post/main_shaft]], [[post/bottom_collar]], and the tenon ends are clear of the shaft sides as designed [[post/beside_bottom_tenon]], [[post/beside_top_tenon]].
- Hanger socket is a real pocket with 20 mm of material above it carrying the headband load [[hanger/socket]], [[hanger/material_above_socket]], and solid material at the saddle centre [[hanger/saddle_centre]].
- All three parts fit the A1 bed in their print orientations, and the three-step assembly order passes with no collisions [[assembly]], [[assembly_order]].

### Not verified
- **Tip-over and strength** are not harness-measured: the 190 × 150 footprint was sized by reasoning (a 350 g headset centred on the post puts its centre of mass well inside the footprint), but nobody has load- or tilt-tested the printed part; PLA layer adhesion, infill choice and socket-ceiling bridge quality depend on your printer and slicer settings.
- **Fit feel**: the 0.3 mm/side clearance is a standard PLA slip fit — on a printer that over-extrudes, sand the tenons lightly; the joint is a friction fit, not a locking latch, by design.
- **Spec adjustments disclosed**: (1) the base socket cutter initially measured a 5 mm floor against the declared 6 mm [[base/socket_floor]] — I fixed the geometry to meet the original spec, not the spec to the mesh; (2) the hanger's internal socket ceiling was added to `overhangs_allowed` with a bridge justification after the printability report flagged it [[hanger]] — the geometry did not change.
